title: Context of the organization
current_state: Leadership understands the business, regulatory and customer context informally.
gap: No documented ISMS scope, internal/external issues or register of interested parties and their requirements.

title: Leadership
current_state: CEO is supportive and the CTO acts as informal security owner.
gap: No approved information security policy, no formally assigned ISMS roles or authorities, and no Information Security Manager.

title: Planning
current_state: This gap assessment is the first structured look at security risk.
gap: No risk assessment methodology, risk treatment plan, Statement of Applicability or measurable security objectives.

title: Support
current_state: Budget and engineering time are available for security tasks on request.
gap: Competence requirements and awareness are not defined, and there is no control of documented information (versioning, approval, retention).

title: Operation
current_state: Several operational controls run because partner banks and PCI DSS require them.
gap: Controls are not planned or operated through a risk treatment plan, and risk assessments are not repeated at planned intervals or after major change.

title: Performance evaluation
current_state: Only uptime and payment-success metrics are tracked.
gap: No security metrics, no internal audit programme and no management review of the ISMS.

title: Improvement
current_state: Problems are fixed when noticed, without root-cause analysis.
gap: No nonconformity and corrective action process or log, and no evidence of continual improvement.
